title: 2-Digit Plus 1-Digit Addition Word Problems
intro: Help your student add ones to a two-digit number using a strategy that fits.
html:
Teaching notes for parents and teachers

How to teach it

Try counting on for a small addition. When the total crosses a ten, show how some of the new ones complete that ten.

Example to work through together

Use the model below as you explain the example. Have your student point to the quantities as you discuss them.

28 counters, then 5 more
2 tens
8 starting ones
5 new ones
Regroup 10 ones as 1 ten
3 tens
3 ones

28 + 5 = 28 + 2 + 3 = 30 + 3 = 33

Use 2 of the 5 new counters to complete a ten. The other 3 stay as ones. The total amount stays the same when the counters are regrouped.

Ask your student

How many more ones are needed to reach the next ten?

If your student needs help

If the student loses track of the amount added, separate the added counters from the starting collection.

Choosing and using the worksheet

These four-problem sets use starting amounts from 10 to 90 and additions from 0 to 9. They include both regrouping and no-regrouping examples across sets, with totals from 10 to 99. They do not include a total of 100, two two-digit addends, or subtraction. Read the short stories aloud when reading would distract from the place-value reasoning.
